importantNotes: Luke is the longest book in the New Testament by word count.
Luke alone records many beloved stories: the Prodigal Son, the Good Samaritan, Zacchaeus.
Luke emphasizes prayer more than any other Gospel — Jesus is frequently shown praying.
Luke highlights the role of women, the poor, and social outcasts in God's plan.
'The Son of Man came to seek and save the lost' (19:10) — the Gospel's purpose statement.

chapters.1: The birth of John the Baptist announced; Gabriel appears to Mary; Mary's song (Magnificat).
chapters.2: The birth of Jesus in Bethlehem; shepherds and angels; presentation at the Temple; boy Jesus.
chapters.3: John the Baptist's ministry; Jesus' baptism; genealogy of Jesus back to Adam.
chapters.4: Jesus tempted in the wilderness; rejected at Nazareth; healings and exorcisms in Capernaum.
chapters.5: The miraculous catch of fish; calling of disciples; healing a leper and a paralytic.
chapters.6: Sabbath controversy; choosing the twelve; the Sermon on the Plain — blessings and woes.
chapters.7: The centurion's faith; raising the widow's son at Nain; John's question; the sinful woman.
chapters.8: The parable of the sower; calming the storm; healing the demoniac; raising Jairus's daughter.
chapters.9: Sending the twelve; feeding 5,000; Peter's confession; Transfiguration; cost of discipleship.
chapters.10: Sending the seventy-two; the Good Samaritan; Mary and Martha.
chapters.11: The Lord's Prayer; teaching on prayer; woes against the Pharisees.
chapters.12: Warnings against hypocrisy and greed; the rich fool; do not worry; be ready.
chapters.13: Repent or perish; the narrow door; lament over Jerusalem.
chapters.14: Healing on the Sabbath; the cost of discipleship; the parable of the great banquet.
chapters.15: Three parables of the lost — the lost sheep, the lost coin, the prodigal son.
chapters.16: The shrewd manager; the rich man and Lazarus; you cannot serve God and money.
chapters.17: Teaching on forgiveness and faith; healing ten lepers; the coming of the kingdom.
chapters.18: The persistent widow; the Pharisee and tax collector; the rich ruler; healing blind man.
chapters.19: Zacchaeus — Jesus seeks and saves the lost; the triumphal entry; cleansing the Temple.
chapters.20: Authority questioned; parable of the tenants; taxes to Caesar; the resurrection debate.
chapters.21: The widow's offering; signs of the end times; the destruction of Jerusalem.
chapters.22: The Last Supper; Gethsemane; betrayal; arrest; Peter's denial; trial before the council.
chapters.23: Jesus before Pilate and Herod; crucifixion; the repentant thief; death and burial.
chapters.24: The resurrection; the road to Emmaus; Jesus appears to the disciples; the ascension.
